about.author: Zyphullen

automatic_checks.what: Structural checks run by a script on every build (src/audit.py, report in AUDIT-v0.9.md): every card has a colour and at least one source, links point at cards that exist, share links are exact, the data hash is the same in every file, counts match, and every source URL was fetched to see that it answers.
automatic_checks.not: They do not read the science. Passing them does not mean a claim is right, only that it is labelled, sourced and linked.

science_review.what: A science review means a person with the right expertise reads each claim against its sources and decides whether it is right, up to date and fairly coloured.
science_review.how_to_help: Every card has a Suggest a fix button (e-mail). Please check claims against the listed sources and say what looks wrong.

about.certainty_rule: green = established (known science, or a defined / proved result in Maths); orange = leading idea / partial progress; red = unknown / open problem. A link takes the colour of its less-certain end.

suggest_a_fix.subject: Echo Atlas fix: <Card name> (<card id>)
suggest_a_fix.note: Every card has a Suggest a fix button that opens a prefilled e-mail (section, card, card id, version, page link). Card ids: fntu/<id>, maths/<id>, history/<id>-<n>, cell/<id>, body/<id>, element/<symbol>, <section>/link/<from>><to>.

about.what_this_file_holds: All 118 elements with symbols, groups and simplified cosmic origins (where each element was mostly made).
about.already_in_this_file: This file already holds everything for this section: the facts (summary, details), the colours (certainty), the sources (title, url, type, year, link check) and the connections between ideas, including links to cards in other sections (rel / related / section_links, each with the other section name and id). Load another section file only when you want the full card on the other end of a link.
about.how_to_use: Every item has id, title, certainty, summary, details and sources (title, url, type). Full source details (year, link check) are in sources_used. A link's reason_sources are the sources on its two cards. Fact-check against the sources; flag anything that looks wrong or out of date.

L.name: Dying low-mass stars
L.note: Giant stars (1–8 Suns) catch neutrons slowly (s-process), then puff off their outer layers. (Most of our lithium: such stars and novae.)

M.name: Massive stars & their supernovae
M.note: Made by fusion, neutron capture and explosive burning in stars >8 Suns; spread by core-collapse supernovae. Includes most Cu and the simpler main-source choice for Zn, Ti and V; shares vary by isotope and remain debated.

W.name: Exploding white dwarfs
W.note: Type Ia supernovae: lots of iron-group metals.

N.name: Merging neutron stars
N.note: Rapid neutron catching (r-process). Maybe also rare supernovae (debated).

R.name: Radioactive decay only
R.note: No long-lived form; made as other elements decay.

H.name: Human-made
H.note: Made in reactors or accelerators (some also in traces or in stars, briefly).

not_yet_made.title: Ununennium (temporary name)
not_yet_made.summary: Not made yet. Hunts running: Dubna (JINR) began Bk-249 + Ti-50 on 1 June 2026, for several months. RIKEN (V-51 + Cm-248) paused after reaching its planned sensitivity, with no atom reported, and is planning its next step.

sources.title: JINR 2026: Dubna starts its element-119 experiment (Bk-249 + Ti-50)
RIKEN (TASCA26 abstract): the V-51 + Cm-248 search for element 119

not_yet_made.title: Unbinilium (temporary name)
not_yet_made.summary: Not made yet. Berkeley showed a Ti-50 beam can make superheavies (2 livermorium atoms in 22 days, 2024); 120 is expected to be 10–20× harder and could take years. ORNL is making a Cf-249 target (2026). An older GSI search (2011) saw one possible chain, never confirmed.

sources.title: US DOE 2025: new progress toward discovering new elements (Ti-50 beam)
Berkeley Lab 2023: testing a new approach to superheavy elements
ORNL talk 2026: Cf-249 target for an element-120 attempt
Hofmann et al. 2016 (EPJ A): GSI search for element 120 (Cr-54 + Cm-248), one unconfirmed chain

not_yet_made.title: Island of stability
not_yet_made.summary: Predicted: nuclei near Z ≈ 114–126 protons and N ≈ 184 neutrons could live much longer than their neighbours. Today's superheavies have too few neutrons to reach it; nobody has made N = 184.

sources.title: Nature Reviews Physics 2023: superheavy elements and the limit of the periodic table
JINR 2026: Ti-50 vs Cr-54 beams for elements 119/120

not_yet_made.title: Where the table may end
not_yet_made.summary: Around Z ≈ 170 the innermost electron level would sink into "negative energy" (estimates 164–174); extended tables stop near 172–173. Nuclei may stop holding together before that.
